stories.title: Google loses long-running appeal of record EU fine, will have to cough up $4.7 billion
stories.author: Ryan Whitwam
bullet_points: Google has lost a major appeal regarding a significant EU antitrust fine.
The fine amounts to $4.7 billion, stemming from anti-competitive practices.

stories.title: Distill to Detect: Exposing Stealth Biases in LLMs through Cartridge Distillation
stories.author: Amin Saberi
bullet_points: The research addresses the critical issue of 'stealth biases' in large language models (LLMs) used in high-stakes applications.
These biases can be introduced anywhere in the model's supply chain and are dangerous because they only manifest on specific topics.
The paper proposes 'Cartridge Distillation' as a method to expose and detect these subtle, context-dependent preferential biases.

stories.title: Distill to Detect: Exposing Stealth Biases in LLMs through Cartridge Distillation

stories.title: Distill to Detect: Exposing Stealth Biases in LLMs through Cartridge Distillation

stories.title: Amazon has enough satellites to launch its Starlink competitor
stories.author: Thomas Ricker
bullet_points: Amazon is advancing its satellite internet venture, Amazon Leo, positioning it as a competitor to SpaceX's Starlink.

This development signals a significant, ongoing push by Amazon into the competitive satellite broadband market.

stories.title: AutoMem: Automated Learning of Memory as a Cognitive Skill
stories.author: Serena Yeung-Levy
bullet_points: Introduces AutoMem, a method to treat memory management as a trainable skill within Large Language Models (LLMs).
Elevates file-system operations to first-class memory actions, allowing the model to autonomously manage its knowledge.
The memory skill improves by optimizing both the underlying structure (prompts, schemas) and the model's actions.

stories.title: FurnitureVLA: Learning Long-Horizon Bimanual Furniture Assembly with Vision-Language-Action Model
stories.author: Diego Romeres
bullet_points: Introduces FurnitureVLA, a novel Vision-Language-Action (VLA) model specifically designed for real-scale bimanual furniture assembly.
Addresses a gap in current research by moving beyond toy-scale or single-arm manipulation to tackle complex, real-world assembly tasks.
Utilizes a comprehensive methodology including scalable simulation pipelines and VR teleoperation for high-quality data collection.

stories.title: World from Motion: Generative Dynamic Gaussian Reconstruction from Monocular Video
stories.author: Alex Trevithick
bullet_points: Introduces 'World from Motion,' a method for creating dynamic, renderable 3D Gaussian representations from standard monocular videos.
The technique conditions a video model on dense, pixel-aligned renderings to accurately encode appearance, geometry, and 3D motion.
It addresses common reconstruction issues like rendering artifacts and missing data by leveraging aligned multiview video pairs for training.

stories.title: Is One Layer Enough? Training A Single Transformer Layer Can Match Full-Parameter RL Training
stories.author: Mingyi Hong
bullet_points: The research challenges the assumption that all transformer layers contribute equally during Reinforcement Learning (RL) fine-tuning of LLMs.
The study systematically investigates layer-wise contributions to RL adaptation in large language models.
A key finding suggests that a single transformer layer can achieve performance comparable to training the entire model with RL.

stories.title: Is One Layer Enough? Training A Single Transformer Layer Can Match Full-Parameter RL Training
stories.author: Mingyi Hong
bullet_points: The research investigates the distribution of Reinforcement Learning (RL) adaptation across different layers of a Transformer model.
It challenges the common assumption that all transformer layers contribute equally during RL post-training.
The study surprisingly demonstrates that a single Transformer layer can achieve performance comparable to training with a full set of parameters.

stories.title: Measuring the Gap Between Human and LLM Research Ideas
stories.author: Arman Cohan
bullet_points: The paper addresses a gap in current LLM evaluation by moving beyond judging individual idea quality (novelty, feasibility).
It introduces a novel framework to measure the conceptual distance between LLM-generated research ideas and those from human researchers.
The methodology involves reverse-engineering prior works from high-quality human papers to establish a baseline for comparison.

stories.title: Language-Critique Imitation Learning from Suboptimal Demonstrations
stories.author: Shao-Hua Sun
bullet_points: Proposes a novel language-critique framework for imitation learning from suboptimal demonstrations.
Addresses the limitation of traditional methods that rely on limited scalar supervision signals (e.g., confidence estimates).
Leverages natural language to explicitly capture intermediate reasoning, failure modes, and corrective actions during learning.

stories.title: Theoria: Rewrite-Acceptability Verification over Informal Reasoning States
stories.author: Michael Saldivar
bullet_points: Theoria is a new verification architecture designed to address the trust gap in AI outputs.
It bridges the gap between the certainty of formal proof assistants and the broad coverage of LLMs.
The system works by rewriting candidate solutions into typed state transitions, each requiring an explicit justification.

stories.title: The State-Prediction Separation Hypothesis
stories.author: Yoav Artzi
bullet_points: Proposes the 'state-prediction separation hypothesis' for Transformer models.
Suggests that separating the token prediction function from the state storage function improves language modeling.
Introduces a new Transformer variant with two computation streams to test this separation.

stories.title: Are Performance-Optimization Benchmarks Reliably Measuring Coding Agents?
stories.author: Lingxiao Jiang
bullet_points: Existing repository-level benchmarks (like GSO, SWE-Perf) are used to evaluate coding agents by applying patches to real codebases.
The current leaderboard scores from these benchmarks may be misleading, potentially conflating runtime instability and specific scoring rules.
The research suggests that the current metrics might overstate the true progress of coding agents due to factors like task saturation in public submissions.

stories.title: Language-Critique Imitation Learning from Suboptimal Demonstrations

Addresses the limitation of previous methods that rely on limited scalar supervision signals (e.g., confidence estimates).

stories.title: Theoria: Rewrite-Acceptability Verification over Informal Reasoning States
stories.author: Michael Saldivar
bullet_points: Theoria is a new verification architecture designed to bridge the gap between formal proof systems and large language model (LLM) outputs.
It addresses the opacity and lack of auditability in current LLM judging methods while overcoming the limited scope of formal proofs.
The system works by rewriting candidate solutions into typed state transitions, each requiring an explicit justification.

stories.title: The State-Prediction Separation Hypothesis
stories.author: Yoav Artzi
bullet_points: Proposes the 'state-prediction separation hypothesis' for Transformers, suggesting that separating the token prediction and state storage functions improves language modeling.
Introduces a novel Transformer variant designed with two distinct computation streams to implement this separation.
Experimental results indicate that state-prediction separation consistently leads to better language modeling performance across different scales.

stories.title: TiRex-2: Generalizing TiRex to Multivariate Data and Streaming
stories.author: Sepp Hochreiter
bullet_points: Introduces TiRex-2, an advanced recurrent xLSTM-based time series foundation model.
Generalizes the original TiRex model to handle multivariate forecasting, incorporating both past and future covariates.
Addresses limitations of existing Transformer models in time series by managing sequential data and avoiding quadratic complexity.

stories.title: Right in the Right Way: LM Training with Verifiable Rewards and Human Demonstrations
stories.author: Jacob Andreas
bullet_points: The paper addresses a limitation in Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable Rewards (RLVR) for Large Language Models (LLMs).
Current RLVR methods focus too heavily on objectively measurable metrics, ignoring subjective qualities like style and structure.
This oversight causes issues like diversity collapse and unnatural outputs in LLM training.

stories.title: Measuring the Gap Between Human and LLM Research Ideas
stories.author: Arman Cohan
bullet_points: The research addresses a gap in evaluating LLM-generated research ideas by comparing them directly to human-led innovation.
A novel evaluation framework is introduced, which reverse-engineers prior works from high-quality human research papers to establish baselines.
The study aims to quantify the 'gap' between the creative output of LLMs and the conceptual leaps made by human researchers.

stories.title: AutoMem: Automated Learning of Memory as a Cognitive Skill

bullet_points: Introduces 'AutoMem,' a framework to treat memory management as a trainable skill within Large Language Models (LLMs).

stories.title: Theoria: Rewrite-Acceptability Verification over Informal Reasoning States
stories.author: Michael Saldivar
bullet_points: Introduces 'Theoria,' a new verification architecture designed to bridge the gap between formal proof assistants and LLM judging.
Theoria converts candidate AI solutions into typed state transitions, each requiring an explicit, auditable justification.
It aims to provide trustworthy AI outputs by addressing the opacity and lack of auditability found in current LLM-based scoring methods.

stories.title: QuasiMoTTo: Quasi-Monte Carlo Test-Time Scaling
stories.author: Emily B. Fox
bullet_points: The paper addresses the high computational cost of scaling language model inference by generating multiple parallel attempts.
Current parallel sampling methods are independent, leading to redundant computation, which the authors argue is not fundamentally necessary.
The proposed QuasiMoTTo method aims to generate correlated but exact samples efficiently, reducing wasted inference compute.

stories.title: Adversarial Pragmatics for AI Safety Evaluation: A Benchmark for Instruction Conflict, Embedded Commands, and Policy Ambiguity
stories.author: Brett Reynolds
bullet_points: The paper introduces a new benchmark focusing on adversarial pragmatics to better evaluate AI safety.
It addresses limitations in current benchmarks that use simple pass/fail labels, failing to distinguish nuanced failure modes.
The benchmark specifically targets complex issues like instruction conflict, embedded commands, and policy ambiguity in LLM behavior.
